turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Hey Dana, you got a sec? The schema migration I ran over the weekend is done.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Oh good, finally. Did you hit any snags? I saw you took the maintenance window on Saturday night.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yeah, used the window like we planned. Honestly, it went smoother than I expected — no locks at all, finished in like 20 minutes.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Nice, that's rare. But wait — did you take a backup before you started? I remember we talked about that last sprint.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Uh... no, I figured it was low risk. The old schema was just a few columns we didn't use anymore.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Sam. You know the rule. No backup, no mercy. But okay, what's done is done. Let's just hope nothing's broken.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Hey, we've got a problem. Customer records are showing up with null addresses for about 300 accounts. That's from your migration, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: What? No way. I only dropped two unused columns. The address field wasn't even touched.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Well, the data says otherwise. Looks like the migration script had a join that silently dropped rows where the old column was null. Classic.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Damn. I really should have backed up. Can we roll back?

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Roll back to what? You didn't take a snapshot. We're going to have to reconstruct from the audit logs. That's going to take days.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I'm an idiot. I'm sorry. I'll start pulling the logs now.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Morning. So, good news: we recovered most of the customer data from the logs. Bad news: we found a regression in production that's been live since Tuesday.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: A regression? What kind? I didn't deploy anything this week except the migration.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Exactly. The migration changed a column type that the payment service relies on. Now some transactions are failing with a type mismatch. It's been happening since you ran it.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Oh no. But I ran the test suite before deploying... wait, no. I didn't. I skipped it because the window was tight.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Yeah, that's what I figured. You deployed without running the tests, and now we've got a regression in prod. We're going to have to do a hotfix and probably a postmortem.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I deserve that. I'll take full responsibility. Let me write the hotfix now — and this time, I'm taking a backup first.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good. And maybe run the tests too, for once.
